11.13.0.en: "If thou put away the iniquity that is in thine hand, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacle" [14].

11.13.1.en: Zophar asks, as his two companions did before him, that Job turn to God with his heart as well as in his practical conduct, bearing neither hypocrisy nor deceit, so that God may answer his prayer.

11.13.2.en: He gave sincere advice about repentance, but we do not know what Zophar's intention was: whether he was truly asking for Job's repentance, or wanted to confirm Job's wickedness and hypocrisy.

11.13.3.en: He asks him to prepare his heart with purity and to stretch out his hands with perseverance in prayer, like one who wants to hold on to God and not let Him go until He blesses him, as our father Jacob did.

11.13.4.en: Zophar demands that he cease from iniquity and drive wickedness out of his tent. A strange demand to a man who dwells on a dunghill, whom the worms clothe like a garment, and who is surrounded by sores from the soles of his feet to his head. What iniquity could he practice with hands that bleed without ceasing? And from what tent could he drive out wickedness when he lives on a dunghill?

11.13.5.en: * Every sin is committed either in thought alone or in thought and deed together. Therefore "the iniquity in thine hand" is iniquity in deed. But "wickedness in the tabernacle" is the injustice in the heart, for our heart is rightly called a tabernacle, in which we are buried within ourselves when our souls do not appear outwardly through deeds.

11.13.6.en: Zophar was the friend of a righteous man and knew what ought to be said, but since he himself bears a likeness to the heretics, in rebuking such a person he does not truly know how to present even what he knows. For he commands us first to remove the iniquity from the hand, and after that to remove the wickedness from the tabernacle. Yet whoever cuts off from himself all outward evil deeds must necessarily return to himself and examine himself wisely as to his heart, lest the sin which is no longer practiced in deed remain behind in thought. Therefore Solomon said well: "Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house" (Prov 24:27). For what does it mean to prepare the work so that the field is diligently made ready outside, except that we uproot the thorns of evil, so that we may work bearing the fruits of reward? And after the field has been plowed, what then is the return to building our house, except that we often learn from good works the complete purity of life that must be built up in our thoughts.

11.13.8.en: * Repentance is given to mankind as grace upon grace. Repentance is a second birth from God, the pledge of which we receive in baptism, and we receive it as a gift through repentance.

11.13.9.en: Repentance is the door of mercy open to all who seek it. Through this door we enter into the divine mercy, and by keeping away from this door no one can find mercy.

11.13.10.en: Since "all have sinned," as the divine Scripture says, [they are justified freely by his grace] (Rom 23:3-24). Repentance is the second grace, born in the heart as the fruit of faith and the fear of God.

11.13.11.en: Fear is the fatherly rod that leads us even to the spiritual Eden, but as soon as we arrive there it leaves us and goes back.

11.13.12.en: Eden is found in divine love, in which is the paradise of all the beatitudes. This is the place where St. Paul received power beyond nature. When he tasted the tree of life he marveled, saying: [Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him] (1 Cor 9:2).

11.13.13.en: St. Isaac the Syrian * There is no sickness that can strike the soul but the word of the Lord offers it a remedy. And just as there are compound medicines which physicians mix and blend to treat bodily diseases, so there are compound medicines prepared by the Spirit of the Lord to treat and confront the passions of sin, so that whoever feels the sickness can find the remedy near him, and enjoy healing.

11.13.14.en: All diseases are healed by their opposites: diseases caused by cold are healed by hot, warming herbs, and diseases caused by heat are healed by moistening herbs...

11.13.15.en: Learn therefore from this, O wise one, you who want your soul's diseases healed, and do for your soul what the science of medicine does for the body. For the things on the outward level have been set before our eyes as an example for us to follow with regard to what touches the inward level, so that our souls are healed in the same way our bodies are healed.

11.13.16.en: Let us then prepare the opposing remedy to meet every passion:

11.13.17.en: against doubt: faith; against error: truth; against suspicion: certainty; against malice: simplicity; against lying: frankness; against deceit: sincerity; against agitation: clarity; against harshness: tenderness; against cruelty: compassion; against fleshly desire: spiritual desire; against pleasure: pain; against the joy of the world: the joy of Christ; against songs: spiritual hymns...

11.13.18.en: and against sorrow: joy; against admiring and boasting of ourselves: sincere hope in God; against fleshly desires: spiritual desires; against the fleshly gaze: the spiritual gaze...

11.13.19.en: and against looking at the things that are seen: thinking on what is unseen...

11.13.20.en: and against attachment to the fleshly family (for the monk): attachment to the heavenly family; and against living in an earthly dwelling: living and dwelling in the heavenly Jerusalem.

11.13.21.en: So all these diseases and their like are healed by their opposites.

11.13.22.en: Whoever longs for the heavenly life must give up earthly, material things, for the desire for one of them does not exist within us unless the other dies. The desire of the Spirit is not born in our thoughts except by the death of the desire of the flesh; by the death of the one the other lives.

11.13.23.en: When the body lives in us with all its desires and wishes, the soul is then dead with all its wishes.

11.14.s.en: 6. There is no escape from divine wrath except by repentance and prayer

11.14.0.en: 15 "For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear: 16 Because thou shalt forget thy misery, and remember it as waters that pass away: 17 And thy lot shall rise above the noonday; the darkness shall turn into morning. 18 And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig about thee, and thou shalt lie down in safety. 19 Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thy face. 20 But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and their refuge shall perish, and their hope shall be the giving up of the soul."

11.14.1.en: "For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear" [15].

11.14.2.en: Here Zophar appears to open the door of hope like his two companions, Eliphaz (Job 8:5 etc.) and Bildad (Job 5:8-7, 20-22), in contrast to Job, over whom, because of the severity of the trial, a pessimistic outlook often prevailed, that his former life would not return!

11.14.3.en: What Zophar said, though it did not suit Job in those circumstances, is nevertheless a true principle for every penitent who is sincere in his repentance. For he cannot lift up his face before the Holy One unless he has removed from himself blemish and shame by the purity of his heart and the holiness of his tabernacle; in this way he stands before God steadfast in his hope and his reliance on God, without fear in his love for God.

11.14.4.en: * If you offer your prayer with a pure heart [13], blameless as to any unseemly deed, then when you offer sighs over yourself before God you come into a meeting with Him. Instead of sorrow you will have joy, and instead of misfortunes you will receive blessings, and the features of your face will be radiant like pure water [15]... and you will no longer fear other afflictions, for God removes the afflictions from you. You will receive pardon for your troubles, and thanksgiving for the calm that settles over you, and you will not fear trials, but will be like one who has found rest in a safe harbor, not fearing the waves where the sea cannot cause harm.

11.14.5.en: Father Hesychius of Jerusalem * Now that we completely wipe away these two (the iniquity of the hand and the wickedness in the tabernacle), we lift up our faces without blemish to God. For the soul is the inner face of man, by which we know our Creator with love and by which we behold Him.

11.14.6.en: Now the lifting up of this very face is the lifting up of the soul to God by the practice of prayer.

11.14.7.en: But the stain that spoils the lifting up of the face is the intention of the deed... For it (the soul) is immediately shattered, and loses all confidence in hope. And when it is occupied with prayer it clings to the remembrance of the sin to which it submitted. It loses confidence in obtaining what it longs for, so it carries in the mind a constant refusal to practice what it hears from God. Therefore John says: "Beloved, if our heart condemn us not, then have we confidence toward God. And whatsoever we ask, we receive of him" (1 Jn 3:21-22). And Solomon says: "He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination" (Prov 28:9). For our heart condemns us in offering our prayers when we remember that they stand against His commandments.

11.14.9.en: * No one is helped by God unless he does something himself. He will be helped if he prays.

11.14.10.en: * The whole effect of faith is this: it makes us ask and receive, seek and find, knock and have it opened to us. Whereas the man who argues shuts the door of God's mercy against himself.

11.14.11.en: * There is no means by which a people attains absolute perfection, or by which any man makes the least progress toward true righteousness and godliness, except by the help of our crucified Savior, Christ, and the gift of His Spirit. Whoever denies this cannot, I think, be counted a Christian at all.

11.14.12.en: St. Augustine "Because thou shalt forget thy misery."

11.15.0.en: "and remember it as waters that pass away" [16].

11.15.1.en: When the sufferer enjoys God's consolations, he forgets his pains and hardship, as a mother forgets the pains of her labor because of her joy over the newborn child. And the sufferings become like a little water poured out of a vessel, leaving no trace of anything.

11.15.2.en: God alone is able to lift the sufferers above their pains, and carry them over them so that they become as nothing, and even turn into countless blessings.

11.15.3.en: "And thy lot shall rise above the noonday."

11.16.1.en: If Job felt that his light had gone out completely, and his life had become like pitch darkness, in Zophar's opinion God will shine His light upon him at his repentance to make of his life a light greater than the light of the sun at noonday, and turn the darkness of night into the joyful light of morning.

11.16.2.en: * [The rising of noonday at evening] is the renewal of virtue in the time of trial... It is written: [Whoso feareth the Lord, it shall go well with him at the last] (Sir 1:13)... The more outward crosses he faces, the more he shines inwardly with the light of his virtues, as Paul bears witness, saying: "though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day. For our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory" (2 Cor 4:16-17).

11.16.5.en: O radiance which no other radiance beholds!

11.16.6.en: You are the light before which all created lights are hidden!

11.16.7.en: You are the radiance before which every outward radiance is extinguished!

11.16.8.en: You are the "light," the source of all lights, and the "radiance," the fountain of all radiance!

11.16.9.en: You are the light and the radiance, before whom all lights become darkness, and every brightness in relation to You is nothing but darkness!

11.16.10.en: You are the radiance by which darkness becomes light, and by which the dark gleams with brilliance!

11.16.11.en: You are the supreme light, no cloud veils You, no vapor hinders You; night is powerless to draw its darkness over You, no barrier obstructs You and no shadows drown You!

11.16.12.en: Finally, You are the light that continually illumines the inner creation; swallow me up in the abyss of Your majesty, that I may behold all Your depths, by the power of the radiance of Your very divinity, and the work of the radiance reflected upon me from You!

11.16.13.en: Never leave me, lest my ignorance increase and my evils multiply, for without You I become empty and wretched!

11.16.14.en: Without You no one has any goodness, for You alone are the truth and the true goodness!

11.16.15.en: This I confess; and this is what I know, O God my God, that wherever I am found without You I have nothing but misery, within as without, for every wealth that is not my God is to me utter poverty!

11.16.16.en: St. Augustine "And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope."

11.17.0.en: "yea, thou shalt dig about thee, and thou shalt lie down in safety" [18].

11.17.1.en: God's consolations remove anxiety from the soul and give it reassurance and peace, as the doors of hope open before it instead of despair.

11.17.2.en: He digs (feels) around him as soldiers do, when they dig trenches and lie down in them in safety, for they rest under the shadow of God's wings, and in Him they enjoy all their needs.

11.17.3.en: * Hope lifts itself with greater steadfastness in God for the hard things that a man suffers for God's sake. The joy of the reward in eternity cannot be gathered unless it is first sown here in godly sorrow. The psalmist says: "He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him" (Ps 126:6). So Paul says: [If we be dead with him, we shall also live with him: if we suffer, we shall also reign with him] (2 Tim 2:11-12). Likewise he warns his disciples, saying: "we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God" (Acts 14:22).

11.17.5.en: * To hope in God from God, this is to love God, the Giver of grace.

11.17.7.en: My God... when will this corrupt nature leave me, and Your perfect power work in me?!

11.17.8.en: My God... sweet is solitude and stillness and truth and purity, all these which are Yours! But I amuse myself with noise and tumult and vanity and vice!

11.17.9.en: Again, what more shall I say?! You are the true Good, merciful, holy, just... but I am wicked, self-loving, sinful, unjust...!

11.17.10.en: You are the light, but I am darkness!

11.17.11.en: You are life, but I am death!

11.17.12.en: You are the Physician, but I am sick!

11.17.13.en: You are joy, but I am sorrow!

11.17.14.en: You are the faithful Truth, but I am true vanity, like any man on the earth!

11.17.15.en: In what language do You wish me to speak to You, my Creator?! I beseech You to be pleased to listen to me. I am the work of Your hands, and my destruction is a fearful thing!

11.17.16.en: I am Your clay, and behold, I am dying! I am the work of Your hands, and behold, I am descending toward nothingness!

11.17.17.en: If I have existence, You are the One who gave me existence, "Thy hands have made me and fashioned me" (Ps 119:73). Your hands which were nailed to the Cross, let them give me peace; for would You despise the work of Your hands?!

11.17.18.en: Ah! I look upon Your deep wounds, for You have engraved my name on Your hands! Read my name and save me!

11.17.19.en: My soul that groans before You is the work of Your hands. Create of me a new creature; this is Your work. Therefore it does not cease to cry out to You, saying: "O Life, make me alive again!"

11.17.20.en: It is the clay of Your hands, it clings around You beseeching You to restore to it its first beauty!

11.17.21.en: Forgive me, my God, since You have allowed me to speak with You. For who is man that he should speak with the Lord his Creator?!

11.17.22.en: Yes. Forgive me! Forgive my boldness! Forgive Your servant who dared to lift his voice before his Master!

11.17.23.en: Necessity knows no law! Pain drives me to speak with You! The disaster that has befallen me makes me call the Physician because I am sick! I seek the light because I am blind! I search for life because I am dead! And who is this Physician and Light and Life but You?!

11.17.24.en: Jesus of Nazareth, have mercy on me!

11.18.0.en: St. Augustine "Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thy face" [19].

11.18.1.en: It is not fitting for a man to be troubled, but to lie down or sleep and rest without disturbance, for he is in the arms of God, surrounded by divine providence.

11.18.2.en: The person becomes not only secure, with no enemies to overcome him and no disasters to shake his being, but many make suit unto his face, for they find peace and consolation in merely looking upon his face. They see the image of the Savior, our Lord Jesus, imprinted on his face, bearing witness to His dwelling in his heart.

11.18.3.en: He who entreats the face of God bears the image of the face of God, and so many entreat him.

11.18.4.en: * Whoever seeks present glory undoubtedly fears contempt. Whoever is always gaping for gain certainly fears loss... But he who is rooted in longing for eternity alone is not exalted by wealth and is not shaken by misfortunes. Since he has nothing in this world that he desires, there is nothing he has to fear from the world.

11.18.5.en: Did not Paul lie down and rest his heart without fear when he said: "For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord" (Rom 8:38-39).

11.18.6.en: The power of this love was praised by the voice of the holy Church when it was said in the Song of Songs: "for love is strong as death" (Song 8:6). Love is compared to the power of death, which, when the soul holds to it, makes it die completely to the delights of the world.

11.19.0.en: "But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and their refuge shall perish (and their refuge shall perish), and their hope shall be the giving up of the soul" [20].

11.19.1.en: After presenting a magnificent picture of pure repentance and its joyful fruit, he warned against evil and its effects. For the eyes of the wicked fail. The eyes that do not look to God, the source of good, are corrupted.

11.19.2.en: "And their hope shall be the giving up of the soul" perishes and vanishes, for "When a wicked man dieth, his expectation shall perish" (Prov 11:7).

11.19.3.en: * By the eyes he means the intention set before us. The Truth bears witness in the Gospel, saying: "If therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light" (Mt 6:22). If the pure intention precedes our deed, then however the deed may appear among men, in the eyes of our inward Judge the deed is counted pure. So the eyes of the wicked are their intentions concerning the fleshly desires within them. These fail because they do not care for their eternal concerns, always looking only toward temporal gains...

11.19.4.en: [And their hope shall be defilement of the soul]. What is the sinner's hope here, in all his thoughts, but to rise above others in power, to have his storehouses surpass the storehouses of all men, to break his rivals in order to rule over them, to satisfy his lust, and to yield in everything to the satisfying of desire? It is well said that their hope is "defilement of the soul."

11.19.5.en: Now it might be said that Zophar is right in this, had not the blessed Job declared this more perfectly through his life.

11.19.7.en: Grant me the living divine truth!

11.19.8.en: * My soul praises You, for You created it in Your image.

11.19.9.en: In its depths it longs to know Your divine truth.

11.19.10.en: Like a bride awaiting the day of her eternal wedding, it wants to adorn itself with the mind of its Bridegroom, and to know His mysteries.

11.19.11.en: * I confess to You, O wondrous Truth!

11.19.12.en: A proud thought has often come over me.

11.19.13.en: I thought myself a defender of You, O Truth, and I took a sword with Peter and struck the opposing servant.

11.19.14.en: In my folly I cut off his spiritual ear, and made him lose the ability to hear Your word!

11.19.15.en: I counted myself a churchman, and in folly I defended her with a strange spirit unworthy of her child!

11.19.16.en: * Grant me the spirit of truth and knowledge, with the spirit of love and tenderness.

11.19.17.en: What truth can I defend without sincere love for all mankind?

11.19.18.en: You came, O Truth, to our wicked world.

11.19.19.en: In bitterness we offered You the Cross, though You are the Lover of all mankind.

11.19.20.en: In folly we defended the truth, and so we persecuted it.

11.19.21.en: Grant me to enjoy You and Your Holy Spirit.

11.19.22.en: For You are the Truth, and You are Love, and You are the Way.

11.19.23.en: Let Your Holy Spirit work in me, the Spirit who is able to convict of sin and to give divine consolations.

11.19.24.en: Grant me the ointment of tenderness and contrition in true humility, that by Your love and tenderness and knowledge I may draw many into the net of Your Church!

11.19.25.en: * Put Your holy words in my mouth, that my tongue may be sanctified and utter only the truth full of love.

11.19.26.en: Speak in me with my tongue, as with my silence.

11.19.27.en: Let me bear witness to the truth in my speeches as in my stillness!

11.19.28.en: * Open Your mouth and speak with me; Your words are light that uncover my darkness and scatter it; grant me enlightenment, so that You save me and glorify me.

11.19.29.en: Teach me how to speak with my brethren, my partners in weakness.

11.19.30.en: Instead of condemnation, let me have compassion on them, so that You may have compassion on me.

11.19.31.en: Let me be weak with their weaknesses, that my heart may be kindled with the fire of Your love.

11.19.32.en: Let me count myself bound as they are bound, and set us all free, O Giver of freedom!

11.19.33.en: * Shine upon me with the light of Your divine wisdom, that I may enjoy a double understanding.

11.19.34.en: Let me perceive Your love through the works of Your surpassing love.

11.19.35.en: And let me discover the secrets of Your care for me, even in the midst of my chastisements.

11.19.36.en: Let me praise You for the generosity of Your gifts; when You give and when You take away, I see You the wonderful God in His care.

11.19.37.en: * Grant me a double wisdom, that I may perceive Your plan, both the manifest and the hidden.

11.19.38.en: And with Your wisdom let me understand the fellowship in the character of Your love.

11.19.39.en: With the double wisdom let me bear a double love.

11.19.40.en: I love You and I love my brethren, who are the object of Your love.

11.19.41.en: * I love You with a double love, I love You with all my heart and soul and might!

11.19.42.en: I know no limits to my love for You!

11.19.43.en: And I love my brethren with a double love; I offer them the spirit of love with generous giving and longsuffering.

11.19.44.en: I do not know how to hate or envy or condemn.

11.19.45.en: I want to treat them as I wish them to treat me.

11.19.46.en: * Grant me, O Lord, a double wisdom, and a double understanding, and a double love.

11.19.47.en: With every morning I enjoy Your new mercies, and I increase in wisdom, understanding and love.

11.19.48.en: I will never be content with what You give me until I become an icon of You.

11.19.49.en: Your gifts kindle my longing for You, and stir up in me fellowship with You and imitation of You, O divine Wisdom and Love!

11.19.50.en: * Grant me, even in rebuking my beloved, to be compassionate!

11.19.51.en: So that my words may be anointed with the anointing of Your Holy Spirit, the Comforter.

11.19.52.en: * I stand before You, O Almighty, and my heart is kindled with longing for more of Your meeting, and my soul groans within me, wanting to know You more.

11.19.53.en: Tell me, if I do not know the secrets of Your visible creation, how dare I claim to know its invisible Creator?

11.19.54.en: If I cannot see the trace of the ship after it has passed, nor the trace of the eagle after it has flown, how can I follow Your trace to know Your plan?

11.19.55.en: * Grant me Your love, in which I may know You and Your plan.

11.19.56.en: Lift my heart by Your Spirit above every vain love, that it may soar always in Your heavens, and know You?

11.19.57.en: Let me know You, that my love for You may increase, and that I may despise all the more every earthly love.

11.19.58.en: * Tell me, where shall I look, O You whom the heavens and the earth cannot contain?

11.19.59.en: I look at heaven, and I long that Your Holy Spirit would fly with me and soar with me in Your heavens, lifting me from glory to glory, until I settle in Your embrace.

11.19.60.en: I contemplate the works of the abyss, and I find that I have no place in it.

11.19.61.en: You descended into it, and broke its bars, and carried me on Your arms, to bring me into the glories.

11.19.62.en: I look at the earth in all its breadth, and it is very narrow for me before the breadth of Your heart toward me and my brethren.

11.19.63.en: I tremble on the shore of the ocean, but its vastness is counted as nothing before the surpassing deep of Your love!

11.19.64.en: Truly, what is the height or depth or length or breadth of Your infinite love!

11.19.65.en: * We rejoice in Your absolute authority, O Love.

11.19.66.en: You are the One who has authority; none can resist, and none can stand before You to question You!

11.19.67.en: But Your authority is the authority of love and tender fatherhood, O Maker of good things.

11.19.68.en: You desire all to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.

11.19.69.en: Your authority is always for edification and glory, as long as we place our lives in Your hands and respond to the grace of Your surpassing goodness.

11.19.70.en: * I confess to You, O Lord, the degradation to which I have sunk.

11.19.71.en: I lost true understanding, and my heart suffered emptiness.

11.19.72.en: Who can fill it but You, O Wisdom of God.

11.19.73.en: Dwell in me, and carry me in You, that I may enjoy You and walk in the wondrous way of wisdom!

11.19.74.en: In You I ascend from the abyss of ignorance, and rise with You to the heavens of wisdom and knowledge.

11.19.75.en: By Your Spirit You continually remove the works of the old man, shatter my ignorance and folly, and renew in me the works of the new man.

11.19.76.en: So that I may truly become an icon of You, O All-wise!

11.19.77.en: * Grant me the life of true repentance; let me turn my back on ignorance and my face toward You, O divine Wisdom.

11.19.78.en: Let me declare my repentance by leaving all evil, and walking in the truth by the riches of Your grace.

11.19.79.en: Lift my heart to You, that I may receive more than I ask, and beyond what I need.
